newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end slightly higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end slightly higher in thin trade.

text.p: Thai stocks made slight gains on Wednesday as close of trade buying took the index into positive territory at the end of a dull afternoon session governed by a lack of political developments.
The SET Index closed at 966.43, up 2.24 points, or 0.23 percent on the day. The SET-50 closed at 74.30 points, up 0.18 points on trade worth 3.44 billion baht.

"The amount of action was very limited, for much of the afternoon it was trading below yesterday's close ... I think it was just waiting for some news to do something different," said Richard Henderson, head of research at Krungthai Thanakit.
Henderson said further shocks to the market may be limited after early week volatility following Sunday's election.
"I think the market is calming down a bit, after a lot of excitement in the last couple of days," he said.
While Thai stocks remain politically sensitive to negotiations underway to form a cabinet, Henderson said he thought support for the market was solidifying.
"I think the background feels okay to me," he said.
Retailers drove trade throughout the day with finance and telecom shares most active, though total market volume was less than half that that of on either Monday or Tuesday.
National Finance gained one baht to 63.50, Bangkok Bank gained two to 206 and Thai Telephone lost 0.50 to 43.25.
